agenda: The situation concerning the Democratic Republic of the Congo; Report of the Secretary-General on the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (S/2025/779)
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: France's primary objectives are to renew MONUSCO’s mandate for twelve months with robust civilian protection provisions, halt the accelerated withdrawal in light of the severe deterioration in North and South Kivu, explicitly demand the withdrawal of Rwandan troops and an end to RDF support for the M23, and firmly endorse the June 2025 Washington Agreement alongside the Luanda and Nairobi processes. The most challenging negotiation points will be balancing explicit naming and demands directed at Rwanda (which the United States and African members may seek to soften or balance against Congolese commitments regarding the FDLR and economic cooperation) versus demands by the DRC and regional actors, as well as calibrating the language on MONUSCO's drawdown timeline.

Algeria.change: Welcoming the peace agreement signed in Washington, D.C., on 27 June 2025 between the DRC and Rwanda, reaffirming the central role and primacy of the African Union-backed Luanda and Nairobi processes, and urging both parties to fully, swiftly, and in good faith implement their commitments in close coordination with African Union and regional mechanisms,

Urges the Governments of the DRC and Rwanda to fully implement the commitments undertaken under the Washington Agreement of 27 June 2025 in synergy with and within the overarching framework of the Luanda and Nairobi processes endorsed by the African Union, including the rapid operationalization of the joint security mechanism to oversee the verified withdrawal of external forces and the cessation of support to and neutralization of the FDLR;

messages.Algeria: Algeria thanks France for circulating this timely draft and fully supports the renewal of MONUSCO's mandate with a robust civilian protection focus. While we welcome recent diplomatic developments, our delegation emphasizes the necessity of anchoring all peace efforts firmly within the African Union-endorsed Luanda and Nairobi frameworks to ensure lasting regional ownership and stability. We also reiterate our unwavering commitment to the full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
messages.China: China supports the extension of MONUSCO's mandate and appreciates the efforts of France as penholder. We believe the Council should firmly uphold the principle of 'African solutions to African problems' by giving prominence to African-led regional mechanisms like the Luanda and Nairobi processes. Additionally, MONUSCO's gradual drawdown must strictly respect the national sovereignty and leadership of the DRC Government, alongside greater attention to addressing the developmental root causes of conflict.
messages.Denmark: Denmark welcomes France's well-balanced draft resolution, which rightly emphasizes MONUSCO's indispensable protection of civilians mandate and reflects the critical developments of the Washington and Luanda processes. We strongly support the extension of the mandate and the clear calls regarding external forces and armed groups. Our proposed adjustments aim to preserve established Council language from resolution 2765 on Women, Peace and Security, Children and Armed Conflict, and climate-related security risks, ensuring a victim-centered and comprehensive approach to civilian protection.
messages.Greece: Greece strongly commends France for a comprehensive and well-calibrated draft resolution that rightly insists on the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC, the conditions-based drawdown of MONUSCO, and full adherence to regional and international peace frameworks. We fully back the renewal of MONUSCO's robust mandate and the draft's clear demands regarding the cessation of external support to armed groups. Our minor textual proposals are aimed at further reinforcing accountability and ensuring explicit focus on the protection of children and the prevention of sexual violence in line with international humanitarian law.
messages.Guyana: Guyana expresses strong support for the draft resolution prepared by France, which rightly defends the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC, calls for the immediate withdrawal of Rwandan forces, and demands the complete neutralization of the FDLR. We appreciate the balanced approach ensuring MONUSCO's conditions-based drawdown while safeguarding civilians and supporting regional frameworks. We propose minor adjustments to reinforce synergy with the African Union Peace and Security Council and highlight protection priorities for women and children.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan thanks France for circulating a comprehensive draft resolution that appropriately balances the extension of MONUSCO's vital mandate with support for the DRC's sovereignty and the ongoing regional peace tracks. As a committed troop-contributing country, we emphasize the utmost necessity of safeguarding peacekeepers and holding accountable those who target them, while ensuring the mission's drawdown remains strictly conditions-based. We also urge the inclusion of language on tracking illicit financial flows from mineral exploitation to effectively tackle the root drivers of conflict in the eastern DRC.
messages.Panama: Panama expresses its strong appreciation to France for preparing this comprehensive and balanced draft resolution, which reflects the critical security developments on the ground and upholds the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. We fully support extending MONUSCO's mandate and ensuring its disengagement remains gradual and conditions-based to prevent any protection vacuum. We suggest minor adjustments to strengthen language on the protection of children, accountability for conflict-related sexual violence, and the meaningful participation of women in peace efforts.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea commends France for drafting a robust and timely resolution that appropriately reflects the grave situation on the ground while anchoring progress in the 27 June Washington Agreement and regional processes. We strongly endorse the extension of MONUSCO's mandate and the draft's clear focus on the protection of civilians and the safety of peacekeepers facing sophisticated threats. We suggest a minor addition to OP 9 to underscore accountability for attacks against peacekeepers, in line with resolution 2589 (2021).
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the renewal of MONUSCO's mandate and the preservation of its core protection responsibilities, in full respect of the sovereignty of the DRC. However, primary emphasis must be placed on African-led diplomatic tracks, namely the Luanda and Nairobi processes, rather than prioritizing external bilateral initiatives. We also caution against overburdening the text with intrusive regulatory language on supply chains that exceeds the Council's purview.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone warmly welcomes France's draft, which robustly addresses the grave security crisis, reinforces MONUSCO's vital mandate, and maintains a responsible, conditions-based disengagement framework. As a consistent champion of African-led solutions, we wish to ensure that regional frameworks—specifically the Luanda and Nairobi processes, the African Union's role, and the Reinforced Ad-Hoc Verification Mechanism (R-AVM)—remain prominently recognized and supported in synergy with the Washington Agreement. We stand ready to work closely with France and all Council members to ensure the swift and unanimous adoption of this text.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia fully supports the renewal of MONUSCO's mandate and commends France for presenting a balanced text that accurately reflects both the political developments and the severe security reality on the ground. We particularly welcome the clear conditions-based approach to mission drawdown and the firm stance on territorial integrity and external interference. Our proposed amendments aim to strengthen protections for children and women, reinforce accountability for grave violations, and enhance the safety of humanitarian personnel in line with international humanitarian law.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the renewal of MONUSCO's mandate and the preservation of DRC's territorial integrity and sovereignty. However, as experience has shown, silencing the guns in Africa is best achieved through regional dialogue and cooperation rather than counterproductive finger-pointing that risks jeopardizing diplomatic momentum. We urge the penholder to place African-led frameworks—specifically the Luanda and Nairobi processes under AU auspices—at the forefront of regional peace efforts and to adopt balanced language regarding the withdrawal of foreign forces.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly welcomes France's draft resolution renewing MONUSCO's vital mandate at this critical juncture, and we fully endorse the firm language upholding the DRC's territorial integrity and demanding the withdrawal of foreign forces and cessation of support to M23. We propose two targeted additions to reinforce our collective response: strengthening the natural resources provisions by referencing the OECD Due Diligence Guidance, and explicitly highlighting the prevention of conflict-related sexual violence and child protection within the Mission's POC priority. We look forward to working closely with France and Council colleagues towards a swift adoption.
messages.United States of America: The United States thanks France for presenting a strong text that accurately reflects conditions on the ground, clearly addresses external interference, and embeds the historic 27 June 2025 Washington Agreement. To ensure durable peace, the Council must support the Washington framework in its entirety, including the critical mineral supply chain and economic integration track alongside the security mechanism. We also believe the resolution should explicitly reiterate our collective readiness to apply targeted 1533 sanctions against those fueling the conflict and plundering Congolese resources.

steps.summary: France has accommodated key member priorities by reinforcing the synergy between the 27 June 2025 Washington Agreement and the AU-backed Luanda and Nairobi processes, strengthening protections for women, children, peacekeepers, and humanitarian workers, and incorporating agreed language on supply chain due diligence, sanctions readiness, and addressing developmental root causes. Firm language regarding DRC sovereignty and the withdrawal of foreign forces was preserved in line with Council findings, ensuring full consensus across the Council.

messages.Algeria: Algeria thanks the penholder for incorporating our proposals into revision 1, particularly reaffirming the overarching importance of African Union-led frameworks and the Luanda and Nairobi processes. We fully support this balanced draft, which upholds the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo while ensuring a responsible, conditions-based approach to MONUSCO's drawdown. Algeria looks forward to voting in favour of the resolution.
messages.China: China thanks France for accommodating our proposals in the revised draft, particularly on respecting the DRC's sovereignty and ownership, upholding African solutions to African problems, and addressing root causes through sustainable development and regional cooperation. We believe the current draft reflects a balanced text that supports peace and stability in the DRC and the Great Lakes region, and we are ready to vote in favour of the resolution.
messages.Denmark: Denmark thanks France for constructive engagement and for incorporating our priorities regarding the protection of civilians, women, peace and security, children in armed conflict, accountability, and climate-related security risks. We fully support this balanced text, which ensures that MONUSCO maintains a robust protection mandate while providing critical backing to regional diplomatic efforts and a responsible, conditions-based transition.
messages.Greece: Greece thanks the penholder for incorporating our proposals reinforcing child protection, the prevention of conflict-related sexual violence, and accountability for war crimes and crimes against humanity. We fully support this balanced text, which firmly upholds the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC and ensures MONUSCO maintains the necessary mandate and operational posture to protect civilians. Greece is ready to vote in favour of the draft resolution as currently formulated.
messages.Guyana: Guyana expresses its appreciation to France for positively addressing our priorities in revision 1, notably by ensuring synergy with African Union-endorsed frameworks and reinforcing dedicated protection for women and children against conflict-related sexual violence. The text provides a balanced, robust, and necessary response to the security and humanitarian crisis while upholding the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Guyana is fully prepared to vote in favour of the draft resolution as currently formulated.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan expresses its appreciation to the French delegation for accommodating our proposals regarding accountability for attacks against UN peacekeepers and the tracking of illicit financial flows. The revised text provides a balanced and robust framework that reaffirms the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo while ensuring that MONUSCO has the necessary mandate and operational posture to protect civilians. Pakistan stands ready to vote in favour of the resolution as drafted.
messages.Panama: Panama commends France for its transparent stewardship as penholder and thanks the delegation for incorporating our proposals regarding the protection of children, combating sexual and gender-based violence, and ensuring women's full and meaningful participation in peace processes. The current draft strikes an appropriate and necessary balance in extending MONUSCO's mandate while reaffirming respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC and supporting ongoing diplomatic frameworks. Panama fully supports the adoption of the draft resolution as presented.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea thanks France for incorporating our proposal on investigating attacks against peacekeepers and ensuring accountability in operative paragraph 9. The revised draft effectively balances MONUSCO's essential protection of civilians mandate with a responsible, conditions-based transition and robust support for regional diplomatic tracks, including the Washington Agreement and the Luanda and Nairobi processes. We fully support the adoption of this resolution.
messages.Russian Federation: We appreciate the penholder's efforts to balance the draft by reaffirming African ownership and the core role of the Luanda and Nairobi regional processes. However, we object to inserting references to non-universal frameworks, namely the OECD Due Diligence Guidance, which lacks universal consensus within the United Nations. With the removal of this reference in OP10, the Russian Federation stands ready to support the adoption of this resolution.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone thanks the penholder for incorporating our proposals into revision 1, particularly reaffirming African leadership through the Luanda and Nairobi processes, the mediation of Angola, and MONUSCO's vital support to the Reinforced Ad-Hoc Verification Mechanism (R-AVM). The current text strikes a balanced and robust approach to addressing the security, humanitarian, and diplomatic dimensions of the crisis while upholding the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Sierra Leone fully supports the draft resolution as revised and looks forward to voting in favour.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia thanks the penholder for accommodating all of our proposals regarding the protection of women and children, the deployment of dedicated protection advisers, and the safeguarding of humanitarian and healthcare personnel. The revised draft effectively balances the urgent need to protect civilians and uphold international humanitarian law with a responsible, conditions-based transition for MONUSCO. Slovenia fully supports the text as currently drafted and looks forward to voting in favour.
messages.Somalia: Somalia thanks the French penholder for accommodating our proposals to anchor the resolution firmly in African-led initiatives, notably the Luanda and Nairobi processes, the African Union framework, and the Reinforced Ad-Hoc Verification Mechanism. While our delegation maintains that sustainable peace in the region is best advanced through dialogue, de-escalation, and regional cooperation rather than stigmatization, we appreciate the overall balance of the text. Somalia fully supports MONUSCO's mandate renewal and stands ready to vote in favour of the draft resolution.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom thanks France for its constructive engagement and for accommodating our proposals on OECD supply chain due diligence and the protection of women and children. Revision 1 provides a robust and balanced framework that ensures MONUSCO can continue its critical protection of civilians mandate while supporting regional peace efforts. The United Kingdom fully supports the text as drafted and looks forward to its swift adoption.
messages.United States of America: The United States thanks France for its constructive stewardship and for incorporating our proposals into Revision 1, particularly regarding the economic integration framework under the 27 June Washington Agreement and the Council's readiness to designate illicit mineral exploiters under the 1533 sanctions regime. This draft accurately reflects the reality on the ground, demands full accountability, and ensures MONUSCO can continue its critical protection of civilians mandate while supporting regional peace efforts. The United States fully supports the text as currently drafted and looks forward to voting in favor.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria consistently supports MONUSCO's mandate, the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and regional diplomatic solutions under African Union auspices. Having supported the draft during negotiations, Algeria votes in favour without a pre-vote explanation.
reasons.China: China has consistently supported MONUSCO's mandate to maintain stability in the DRC, respects the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC, and endorsed the draft resolution in negotiations, with explanations of vote traditionally delivered after adoption.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark fully supports the renewal of MONUSCO's mandate, the focus on the protection of civilians, human rights, international humanitarian law, and a conditions-based withdrawal. As an elected member supportive of the French-penned text, Denmark votes in favour and reserves any remarks for after the adoption.
reasons.France: As the penholder and sponsor of the draft resolution renewing MONUSCO's mandate, France fully supports the text and votes in favour while delivering introductory remarks to encourage unanimous Council adoption.
reasons.Greece: Greece consistently supports MONUSCO's peacekeeping mandate, the preservation of DRC's sovereignty and territorial integrity, and alignment with EU partners including the penholder France, seeing no need to take the floor before the vote.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana consistently supports MONUSCO's mandate renewal, the protection of civilians, respect for the DRC's sovereignty and territorial integrity, and regional peace frameworks, aligning fully with its established voting record and A3+ coordination.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan is a consistent supporter of MONUSCO, a major troop-contributing country, and strongly upholds the DRC's sovereignty and territorial integrity while supporting regional peace mechanisms. In line with its established practice and its position during negotiations, Pakistan votes in favour of renewing MONUSCO's mandate and reserves its remarks for after the vote.
reasons.Panama: Panama consistently supports MONUSCO's mandate, territorial integrity of the DRC, and diplomatic efforts to resolve the conflict, aligning fully with the draft resolution submitted by France. As is standard practice when voting in favour, Panama does not need to deliver an explanation of vote prior to the voting procedure.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea consistently supports MONUSCO's mandate renewal and peace efforts in the DRC, aligning with our stance throughout previous resolutions and negotiations. We will vote in favour of the draft resolution and reserve any remarks for after the vote.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia consistently supports the renewal of MONUSCO's mandate and respect for the DRC's sovereignty, and our key negotiation priority—removing non-consensual references to OECD guidelines in OP10—was accommodated by the penholder. In line with Council practice on this file, any explanation of vote will be delivered after the adoption.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone consistently supports MONUSCO mandate renewals, prioritizes the protection of civilians and DRC sovereignty, and backs African-led diplomatic frameworks. As a key A3 member and frequent co-sponsor on DRC issues, Sierra Leone votes in favour and delivers a pre-vote statement affirming its commitment.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia consistently supports MONUSCO's mandate renewal, with a strong focus on the protection of civilians, international humanitarian law, human rights, and regional peace frameworks, and in line with our consistent voting record on the DRC, we vote in favour. As an elected member supporting the draft, an explanation of vote before the adoption is unnecessary.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia supports the renewal of MONUSCO's mandate and the protection of civilians in eastern DRC, particularly with our requested language commending President João Lourenço's mediation under the Luanda process incorporated into operative paragraph 8.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly supports extending MONUSCO's mandate and the draft resolution's calls for an end to external support for armed groups, full respect for the DRC's sovereignty, and adherence to the Washington and Luanda peace frameworks.
reasons.United States of America: The draft resolution aligns directly with United States foreign policy priorities by extending MONUSCO's mandate, explicitly demanding the withdrawal of Rwandan forces and the cessation of DRC support to the FDLR, and welcoming the US-brokered Washington Agreement of 27 June 2025. Consistent with our established voting record, the United States votes in favour and will deliver its remarks after the vote.

before.France:
Monsieur le Président,

France, as the penholder on this file, has submitted the draft resolution before us today to renew the mandate of the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO) for an additional year.

The situation in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo remains deeply alarming. Civilians continue to bear the unbearable brunt of violence committed by armed groups, including the M23, the FDLR, the ADF, and CODECO, resulting in massive displacement and an acute humanitarian crisis. 

This draft resolution sends a clear and united message: there can be no military solution. The sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo must be fully respected. All external support to armed groups must cease immediately, and Rwandan forces must completely withdraw from Congolese territory, just as the Congolese authorities must end any cooperation with the FDLR. 

In this exceptionally difficult environment, MONUSCO’s presence remains indispensable for the protection of civilians and the facilitation of humanitarian aid. This resolution extends the Mission’s mandate while reaffirming that any future disengagement must remain gradual, responsible, and closely calibrated to the security realities on the ground in full partnership with the Congolese Government. It also anchors Council support for ongoing diplomatic initiatives, notably the 27 June Washington Agreement and the Luanda and Nairobi processes.

France expresses its sincere gratitude to all Council members for their constructive engagement throughout negotiations, and we urge all delegations to vote in favour of this draft resolution.

Je vous remercie.
before.Sierra Leone:
Sierra Leone wishes to express its full support for the draft resolution before us today renewing the mandate of the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO). 

The catastrophic security and humanitarian situation in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, exacerbated by the relentless violence and territorial expansion of the M23 and other armed groups, demands the continued, unwavering commitment of this Council. The protection of civilians remains paramount, and MONUSCO’s presence and proactive posture are vital in preventing further atrocities and safeguarding vulnerable populations, particularly women and children. 

Sierra Leone reaffirms its steadfast commitment to the sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. There can be no military solution to this crisis. Lasting peace can only be achieved through political dialogue, the immediate cessation of hostilities, the complete withdrawal of all unauthorized foreign forces, and the end of external support to armed groups. 

We strongly welcome the synergy between diplomatic initiatives, notably the African Union-led Luanda and Nairobi processes and the 27 June Washington Agreement. Sierra Leone firmly believes that African-led solutions, supported by international partnership, provide the indispensable framework for addressing the root causes of instability in the Great Lakes region. 

Furthermore, we support a gradual, responsible, and conditions-based withdrawal of MONUSCO, undertaken in close consultation with the Congolese authorities, to ensure that no security vacuums are created that could further endanger civilians. 

For these reasons, Sierra Leone will vote in favour of the draft resolution and urges all members to do likewise.

after.Algeria:
Mr. President,

Algeria voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, extending the mandate of the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO). We wish to thank the penholder, France, for its constructive engagement and dedication throughout the negotiation process to maintain the unity and consensus of this Council.

My delegation reaffirms its steadfast and unwavering commitment to the sovereignty, unity, independence, and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, as well as the principle of non-interference in the internal affairs of States. 

Algeria remains deeply alarmed by the persistent violence and the grave deterioration of the security and humanitarian situation in the eastern provinces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, particularly in North Kivu, South Kivu, and Ituri. The intolerable suffering inflicted upon millions of Congolese civilians, the dramatic surge in internal displacement, and widespread violations of international humanitarian and human rights law—especially against women and children—require urgent, resolute, and concerted action by the international community.

We reiterate our firm condemnation of the military offensives and abuses committed by the M23 and all other armed groups, including the FDLR, the ADF, and CODECO. We demand that all armed groups immediately cease hostilities, permanently withdraw from all occupied areas, and disarm unconditionally. Furthermore, we reiterate that any external support to armed groups must end immediately, and we demand the complete withdrawal of all unauthorized foreign forces from Congolese territory. 

Algeria firmly believes that there is no military solution to the conflict in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. Sustainable peace can only be achieved through a comprehensive political solution that addresses the root causes of the instability. In this regard, we reiterate our full support for the principle of "African solutions to African problems." We emphasize the centrality of the regional peace efforts endorsed by the African Union, in particular the harmonized Luanda and Nairobi processes under the auspices of the African Union and the mediation of Angola. We also take note of recent diplomatic initiatives, including the agreement signed in Washington, and urge all parties to implement their commitments fully, swiftly, and in good faith.

In conclusion, Algeria pays tribute to the bravery and dedication of MONUSCO personnel and troop- and police-contributing countries who carry out their duties under increasingly perilous conditions. The Mission plays an essential role in the protection of civilians and the stabilization of the country. We call on all parties to respect MONUSCO’s mandate and guarantee the safety and security of peacekeepers and humanitarian personnel at all times.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.China:
Mr. President,

China voted in favour of the resolution just adopted extending the mandate of the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO). We commend France, as the penholder, for its efforts in facilitating consultations on this text.

China has consistently supported MONUSCO in playing an active and constructive role in maintaining peace and stability in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The current security and humanitarian situation in the eastern DRC remains grave and complex. We express our deep concern over the ongoing violence and the severe suffering endured by the civilian population. China reiterates that the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo must be earnestly respected by all parties. 

We urge the M23 and all other armed groups to immediately cease hostilities, halt all territorial expansion, withdraw from occupied areas, and disarm unconditionally. External parties must immediately end all unauthorized military presence and support to armed groups in the DRC.

There is no military solution to the conflict in eastern DRC. Dialogue and consultation are the only viable path to lasting peace. China welcomes all diplomatic efforts aimed at easing tensions, including the peace agreement signed in Washington in June, and calls on the parties concerned to implement their commitments in good faith. At the same time, China reiterates its consistent support for solving African issues through African solutions. We support the African Union and regional mechanisms in continuing to play a leading role, and we call on the international community to continue backing the Luanda and Nairobi processes.

China hopes that MONUSCO will continue to strengthen communication and coordination with the Government of the DRC, carry out its mandate in accordance with the principles of peacekeeping, and focus its efforts on protecting civilians and supporting regional de-escalation. Moving forward, the Mission's drawdown and transition must proceed in a gradual, responsible, and coordinated manner, fully taking into account the security situation on the ground and respecting the ownership of the DRC Government.

Achieving durable peace and stability in eastern DRC requires addressing both symptoms and root causes, including tackling the illegal exploitation and illicit trade of natural resources, promoting sustainable development, and improving people’s livelihoods. China stands ready to work with the international community to continue playing a constructive role in supporting the DRC and the Great Lakes region in achieving long-term peace, stability, and development.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Denmark:
Thank you, Mr. President.

Denmark voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, renewing the mandate of MONUSCO for an additional year. We thank France for its constructive leadership as penholder.

The ongoing violence and human suffering in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo remain deeply alarming. Millions of civilians continue to endure devastating levels of displacement, food insecurity, and human rights abuses at the hands of armed groups, including the M23, the FDLR, the ADF, and CODECO. We condemn these attacks in the strongest terms.

Denmark reiterates its unequivocal commitment to the sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity of the DRC. Any external support to armed groups must cease immediately. Rwandan forces must withdraw completely and unconditionally from Congolese territory, and all operational support to the FDLR must end. Lasting peace cannot be achieved through military escalation. We urge all parties to honour their commitments under regional and international frameworks, including the Luanda and Nairobi processes and the agreement signed in Washington earlier this year.

For Denmark, the protection of civilians remains the paramount priority of MONUSCO. We are particularly horrified by the dramatic rise in conflict-related sexual violence and grave violations committed against children. Accountability for these atrocities is non-negotiable; perpetrators of war crimes and violations of international humanitarian law must be held to account. 

Finally, Denmark pays tribute to the dedication and sacrifice of MONUSCO’s personnel and troop- and police-contributing countries. All parties must guarantee the safety and security of peacekeepers and ensure rapid, safe, and unhindered humanitarian access to all those in need.

Thank you.
after.Greece:
Mr. President,

Greece welcomed the unanimous adoption of the resolution renewing the mandate of MONUSCO for an additional year, and we express our appreciation to the penholder, France, for its dedicated efforts in facilitating this consensus.

Our vote in favour reflects Greece’s steadfast and unwavering commitment to the principles of the United Nations Charter, paramount among which are full respect for the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and political independence of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, as well as the principle of non-interference. 

The security and humanitarian situation in eastern DRC remains deeply alarming. Millions of civilians continue to endure devastating violence, displacement, and acute suffering. We reiterate our unequivocal condemnation of the offensives, atrocities, and human rights violations committed by armed groups, notably the M23, the FDLR, the ADF, and CODECO. All armed groups must immediately cease hostilities, permanently vacate all occupied territories, and disarm unconditionally. 

Furthermore, we stress that any external support to armed groups must end immediately. The unauthorized presence of foreign military forces on Congolese territory violates international law and must cease without delay, as their full and unconditional withdrawal is essential for de-escalation and regional stability. 

Greece places the protection of civilians at the very core of peacekeeping mandates. We are gravely concerned by the dramatic rise in conflict-related sexual violence and grave violations against children in eastern DRC. There can be no impunity for war crimes, crimes against humanity, and violations of international humanitarian law; perpetrators must be held fully accountable. 

We commend the brave men and women of MONUSCO who operate under increasingly perilous conditions. Attacks, threats, and technological harassment against peacekeepers, including the use of surface-to-air missiles and GPS jamming, are completely unacceptable, endanger civilian and humanitarian aviation, and must be strongly condemned. 

Finally, lasting peace cannot be achieved solely through military means. We welcome the peace agreement reached in Washington on 27 June 2025, alongside the vital efforts undertaken through the African Union-endorsed Luanda and Nairobi processes. We urge all parties to honour their commitments fully, swiftly, and in good faith to bring genuine peace and security to the people of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the wider Great Lakes region.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Guyana:
Mr. President,

Guyana voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, extending the mandate of the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO) for a further year. We express our appreciation to France, the penholder, for its constructive engagement and dedication throughout the negotiation process.

Guyana remains deeply alarmed by the persistent insecurity and devastating humanitarian catastrophe in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. The ongoing violence, territorial aggression, and abuses perpetrated by armed groups—including the M23, the FDLR, the ADF, and CODECO—continue to exact an unconscionable toll on innocent civilians, particularly women and children who endure the brunt of displacement and conflict-related sexual violence.

Today’s renewal reaffirms the critical role played by MONUSCO in the protection of civilians and the stabilization of the country. Guyana pays tribute to the dedication, bravery, and sacrifice of the Mission's peacekeepers, and we strongly condemn any attacks, threats, or obstruction aimed at UN personnel and operations.

Guyana reiterates its steadfast commitment to the sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. We reiterate our demand for the M23 and all other armed groups to immediately cease hostilities, halt their advances, and disarm unconditionally. We reiterate our call for the immediate, unconditional, and complete withdrawal of all Rwandan Defence Forces from Congolese territory, as well as the complete cessation of any support to armed groups. Likewise, we urge the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo to end all collaboration with and vigorously pursue the neutralization of the FDLR. 

There can be no military solution to this protracted conflict. Lasting peace can only be achieved through genuine political dialogue and faithful adherence to commitments. In this regard, we welcome the regional and international diplomatic efforts, notably the Luanda and Nairobi processes and the peace agreement signed in Washington on 27 June 2025. We urge all parties to implement their obligations swiftly, comprehensively, and in good faith.

Guyana stands in full solidarity with the Government and people of the Democratic Republic of the Congo in their quest for enduring peace, stability, and prosperity.

I thank you.
after.Pakistan:
Mr. President,

Pakistan voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, which extends the mandate of the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO) for an additional year. We thank France, as the penholder, for its efforts in facilitating consultations and steering the Council towards a unanimous outcome.

The eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to endure an alarming cycle of violence, marked by severe human suffering, mass displacement, and an acute humanitarian crisis. The persistent offensives by armed groups, notably the M23, as well as the activities of the FDLR, ADF, CODECO, and other militias, pose a grave threat not only to the civilian population but also to regional peace and stability. 

Pakistan reaffirms its steadfast commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. We reiterate that all external support to armed groups must cease immediately and unconditionally, and all unauthorized foreign forces must withdraw from Congolese territory. At the same time, existing commitments to neutralize and disarm hostile armed groups must be faithfully implemented.

As a consistent and leading troop-contributing country to United Nations peacekeeping operations, including in the DRC over many years, Pakistan attaches paramount importance to the safety, security, and operational effectiveness of MONUSCO personnel. We strongly condemn all attacks, threats, and technological obstruction directed against peacekeepers and humanitarian actors, including the reckless deployment of advanced weaponry and electronic warfare assets. Peacekeepers must be provided with the necessary political backing, clear mandates, and adequate resources to carry out their primary priority: the protection of civilians.

Any future drawdown or reconfiguration of MONUSCO must remain gradual, responsible, and strictly condition-based, carried out in full consultation with the Government of the DRC to prevent any security voids that armed groups could exploit.

Finally, Pakistan underlines that a sustainable resolution of the conflict in eastern DRC requires addressing its root causes, including the illegal exploitation and illicit trade of natural resources. There can be no purely military solution. We welcome the diplomatic momentum generated by recent peace initiatives, including the Washington agreement, and reaffirm our support for regional peace efforts through the Luanda and Nairobi processes. We urge all parties to engage in good faith to silence the guns and bring lasting peace and dignity to the people of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Panama:
Panama welcomes the unanimous adoption of the resolution extending the mandate of the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO), and we thank the delegation of France for its constructive efforts as penholder in achieving consensus.

Our vote in favour reaffirms Panama’s unwavering commitment to the sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, as well as our firm support for MONUSCO and its peacekeepers, who continue to carry out their essential work under exceptionally difficult and dangerous conditions. The mission's mandate to protect civilians remains vital, particularly in the face of acute humanitarian suffering, widespread displacement, and unacceptable violations of human rights and international humanitarian law, which disproportionately affect women and children.

The volatile situation in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo cannot be resolved by military means. We reiterate our call for the immediate cessation of hostilities, the complete withdrawal and disarmament of the M23 and all other armed groups, and the immediate and unconditional withdrawal of all unauthorized foreign forces from Congolese territory. 

We urge all parties to fully honour their commitments under international law and to implement the agreements reached, including the Washington peace agreement of June 2025, alongside the Luanda and Nairobi processes. Sustainable peace can only be achieved through genuine political dialogue, regional cooperation, and respect for international law.
after.Republic of Korea:
Thank you, Mr. President.

The Republic of Korea voted in favour of the resolution extending the mandate of MONUSCO for an additional year. We commend France, the penholder, for its dedicated efforts in guiding the Council to achieve unity on this critical text today.

The persistent and catastrophic violence in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to exact an unacceptable toll on millions of innocent civilians. The dramatic rise in civilian casualties, mass displacement, and egregious violations—particularly conflict-related sexual violence and grave violations against children—demands our collective and unwavering attention.

My delegation reiterates our strong commitment to the sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity of the DRC. There can be no military solution to this crisis. All armed groups, including the M23, the FDLR, the ADF, and CODECO, must immediately lay down their weapons, cease all hostilities, and disarm unconditionally. Furthermore, all external support to these armed groups must end, and any unauthorized foreign military forces must immediately and completely withdraw from Congolese territory.

We welcome the diplomatic momentum generated by recent peace initiatives, including the 27 June Washington agreement, alongside the vital efforts led by the African Union, the Luanda and Nairobi processes. We urge all parties to implement their commitments fully, swiftly, and in good faith to de-escalate tensions and restore stability to the Great Lakes region.

Under these extremely perilous circumstances, MONUSCO’s presence remains vital. The Republic of Korea pays profound tribute to the courage and sacrifice of MONUSCO peacekeepers. We strongly condemn all attacks, threats, disinformation, and dangerous acts of obstruction against the Mission, including the use of advanced weaponry and GPS jamming that endanger peacekeepers, civilian aviation, and humanitarian workers. All parties must guarantee full, safe, and unhindered humanitarian access and respect the safety and security of United Nations personnel.

As our term on the Security Council draws to a close, the Republic of Korea reaffirms its steadfast commitment to peace, stability, and the protection of civilians in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and across the Great Lakes region.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation voted in favour of the resolution submitted by France to extend the mandate of the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO).

Our vote reflects Russia’s consistent and principled position in support of the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The protracted and deeply alarming crisis in the eastern provinces continues to take a severe toll on the civilian population. Millions of people have been displaced, and the humanitarian situation remains catastrophic. 

We condemn the violent actions and offensives of all illegal armed groups operating in eastern DRC, including the M23, the FDLR, the ADF, CODECO, and others. It is imperative that all armed formations immediately cease hostilities, lay down their weapons, and participate unconditionally in disarmament, demobilization, and reintegration programmes.

Russia has consistently maintained that there is no military solution to the conflict in the Great Lakes region. Sustainable peace can only be achieved through political and diplomatic dialogue. In this context, we emphasize the primary importance of African-led diplomatic initiatives, notably the Luanda and Nairobi processes under the auspices of the African Union and the mediation of Angola. We reaffirm our firm commitment to the principle of “African solutions to African problems.” While taking note of the agreements reached with external facilitation, including in Washington, we stress that any lasting settlement must be firmly anchored in regional ownership and genuine respect for the security interests and sovereignty of all States in the region.

Under the current complex security conditions, the presence of MONUSCO remains an essential stabilizing factor, particularly for the protection of civilians and the facilitation of humanitarian aid. We pay tribute to the peacekeepers who carry out their duties under perilous circumstances and condemn all attacks and provocations directed against Mission personnel and assets. 

At the same time, we would like to reiterate our well-known position: the Council must avoid overloading the mandates of peacekeeping operations with extraneous issues that dilute their core focus, including attempts to artificially link security issues to the climate agenda. The effectiveness of MONUSCO depends first and foremost on close, constructive cooperation and mutual trust with the host Government in Kinshasa, as well as on assisting the Congolese authorities in restoring State authority and strengthening their own national security forces.

Thank you.
after.Slovenia:
Mr. President,

Slovenia voted in favour of the resolution renewing the mandate of MONUSCO for another year, and we thank France as the penholder for its balanced and constructive leadership throughout the negotiations.

Our vote reflects Slovenia’s unwavering commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and political independence of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It also reaffirms our resolute support for MONUSCO and its indispensable role, above all in the protection of civilians under imminent threat.

The humanitarian and security crisis in eastern DRC remains alarming. Millions of people have been displaced, and innocent civilians—particularly women and children—continue to bear the heaviest toll of violence. Slovenia condemns in the strongest terms the persistent attacks, abuses, and territorial expansion carried out by armed groups, notably the M23, the FDLR, the ADF, and CODECO. We reiterate our call for all armed groups to immediately cease hostilities, lay down their weapons, and participate unconditionally in disarmament processes.

We also stress that all external support to armed groups must end immediately. The unauthorized presence of Rwandan forces on Congolese territory violates international law and must cease without delay. Equally, any operational support or cooperation between state armed forces and groups such as the FDLR must be completely halted. 

Accountability is paramount. The dramatic rise in conflict-related sexual violence and grave violations against children in eastern DRC is unconscionable. Perpetrators of war crimes, crimes against humanity, and violations of international humanitarian law must be held to account. Impunity cannot be tolerated.

Slovenia also underscores the urgent need to guarantee safe, rapid, and unhindered humanitarian access to all populations in need. Furthermore, we condemn any targeting, harassment, or technological disruption, including GPS jamming and the use of advanced weaponry, aimed at peacekeepers and humanitarian actors. The safety and security of United Nations personnel must be guaranteed at all times.

Finally, there can be no purely military solution to this conflict. We welcome the diplomatic engagements under the Luanda and Nairobi processes, as well as the Washington agreement, and urge all parties to implement their commitments in full and in good faith. 

Slovenia remains dedicated to supporting the people of the Democratic Republic of the Congo on their path toward sustainable peace, justice, and stability.

I thank you.
after.Somalia:
Mr. President,

Somalia voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, extending the mandate of the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO) for an additional year.

My delegation reiterates its deep concern over the continuing deterioration of the security, human rights, and humanitarian situation in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. The suffering inflicted upon the civilian population, particularly women and children, through mass displacement, violence, and acute food insecurity, demands the sustained attention and unity of this Council.

We reaffirm our steadfast commitment to the sovereignty, unity, independence, and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, as well as all States in the region. Respect for these foundational principles, along with non-interference and good-neighbourliness, is essential for any enduring peace. 

As we have consistently maintained, experience has shown that silencing the guns in Africa does not begin with finger-pointing or attributing blame, but through genuine political will, inclusive dialogue, and regional cooperation. While armed groups must immediately cease hostilities, lay down their weapons, and unconditionally disarm, there can be no purely military solution to this protracted conflict. 

In this regard, Somalia welcomes all constructive diplomatic efforts aimed at de-escalation, including the peace agreement reached in Washington in June, and underscores the primary importance of regional frameworks. We reaffirm our full support for the African Union-led Luanda and Nairobi processes, and commend the tireless mediation efforts of President João Lourenço of Angola. Regional ownership and the principle of African solutions to African problems remain central to resolving the underlying causes of instability. We urge all parties to implement their commitments in good faith and without delay.

Finally, my delegation pays tribute to the men and women of MONUSCO, as well as the troop- and police-contributing countries, for their courage and dedication in implementing the Mission’s mandate and protecting vulnerable civilians under increasingly perilous conditions. 

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
The United Kingdom welcomes the unanimous adoption of today’s resolution renewing the mandate of MONUSCO, and we thank France for its dedicated leadership as penholder.

The ongoing conflict and worsening humanitarian catastrophe in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo demand our sustained and resolute attention. Millions of civilians have been displaced, and we remain appalled by the horrific levels of violence against civilians, including grave violations against children and widespread conflict-related sexual violence. Those responsible for these egregious abuses must be held fully accountable.

There is no military solution to this crisis. The sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo must be respected. We reiterate our unequivocal condemnation of the offensives and abuses committed by M23 and other armed groups, and demand that M23 cease all hostilities and withdraw from all occupied areas. 

We also reiterate our call for the immediate, unconditional, and complete withdrawal of all Rwandan Defence Forces from Congolese territory and an end to all external support to armed groups. Equally, the DRC Government must cease all collaboration with the FDLR and pursue their complete neutralization. 

Diplomatic engagement remains the only viable path to lasting peace. We urge the parties to implement their commitments under the 27 June Washington agreement swiftly and in good faith, in close coordination with the regional Luanda and Nairobi processes.

Finally, the United Kingdom pays tribute to the bravery and dedication of MONUSCO peacekeepers operating in increasingly perilous conditions. Any attacks, threats, or obstruction against the Mission—including the dangerous use of advanced weaponry and electronic interference—are wholly unacceptable and must cease immediately. MONUSCO must be granted the full operational freedom and support required to deliver on its vital protection of civilians mandate.
after.United States of America:
Thank you, Mr. President.

The United States was pleased to vote in favor of today’s resolution renewing the mandate of the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO) for an additional year. We thank France for its leadership as penholder and for its constructive engagement throughout negotiations.

Today’s unanimous adoption sends an unequivocal message of international resolve at a critical juncture for the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the broader Great Lakes region. The millions of Congolese civilians who have endured unimaginable violence, displacement, and acute human rights abuses must not be forgotten. MONUSCO’s mandate to protect civilians, support state authority, and facilitate humanitarian access remains indispensable. We honor the bravery and sacrifice of MONUSCO peacekeepers who carry out their duties under increasingly dangerous and hostile conditions.

The resolution adopted today rightly reflects the facts on the ground. We welcome the Council’s clear, explicit condemnation of the unauthorized presence and military operations of the Rwandan Defence Forces on Congolese territory and the demand for their complete, immediate, and unconditional withdrawal. We also reiterate our utter condemnation of the offensives, territorial expansion, and horrific abuses committed by the M23. M23 must immediately cease all hostilities, vacate all occupied areas, and disarm unconditionally. At the same time, we reaffirm that the Government of the DRC must cease all collaboration with and operational support to armed groups, including the FDLR, and pursue the complete neutralization and disarmament of the FDLR. 

There is no military solution to this conflict. Lasting peace can only be achieved through genuine political will and dialogue. The historic agreement signed in Washington on June 27, 2025, between the DRC and Rwanda—facilitated by the United States—alongside the regional Luanda and Nairobi processes, provides a concrete pathway toward sustainable de-escalation, regional economic integration, and respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity. Both parties must honor their commitments fully, swiftly, and in good faith, including through the joint security mechanisms and verified withdrawal timelines. 

The United States remains steadfastly committed to supporting the people of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, ending the cycle of impunity and the illicit exploitation of natural resources fueling this conflict, and achieving enduring stability and prosperity across the Great Lakes region. 

Thank you, Mr. President.
